LESSON OBJECTIVE
Read, draw, and compare box plots using the five-number summary; calculate range, IQR, and whisker lengths, and interpret the middle 50%.
CORE IDEA
A box plot compresses a distribution into five ordered landmarks: minimum, Q1, median (Q2), Q3, and maximum. The box shows the middle half of the data.
KEY DEFINITIONS
Minimum and maximum are the extremes; Q1 and Q3 mark the 25th and 75th percentiles; the median marks the center. A whisker connects a box edge to an extreme in a basic box plot.
CORE RULE
Five-number summary: min ≤ Q1 ≤ median ≤ Q3 ≤ max. IQR=Q3−Q1; range=max−min; lower whisker=Q1−min; upper whisker=max−Q3.
HOW IT WORKS

Sort the data. Find the median; find Q1 and Q3 as medians of lower and upper halves (exclude the central observation for odd n). Draw a number line, whiskers at min/max, a box from Q1 to Q3, and a median line.
WORKED EXAMPLE 1 — READ THE BOX
A plot has min=2, Q1=5, median=9, Q3=13, max=16. Read the box edges as 5 and 13 and the median line as 9. Its IQR is 13−5=8.
WORKED EXAMPLE 2 — COMPARE SPREAD
Plot A has Q1=3, Q3=9; plot B has Q1=5, Q3=14. IQR(A)=6, IQR(B)=9. B has 3 units more spread among the middle half.
WORKED EXAMPLE 3 — WHISKERS
For summary (3,7,11,16,25), the lower whisker is 7−3=4 and upper whisker is 25−16=9. The upper tail extends 5 units farther.
WORKED EXAMPLE 4 — TRANSLATION
If all scores increase by 5, the entire box plot shifts right by 5. Median 10 becomes 15, but range and IQR remain unchanged.
WORKED EXAMPLE 5 — SCALE AND OUTLIERS
For Q1=7, Q3=17, IQR=10; the upper 1.5×IQR fence is 17+15=32. A value above 32 may be an outlier. Multiplying all values by 3 triples whisker lengths and IQR.

COMMON MISTAKES

Do not read the width of the box in screen pixels: use the number-line scale. Do not mistake the median line for the mean. A longer whisker means a longer numeric tail, not necessarily more observations.
EXAM STRATEGY

Read the five landmarks first. For IQR use the box edges; for range use the whisker endpoints. Compare two plots using the same horizontal scale. State whether the question asks about center, spread, or possible outliers.
QUICK CHECK
If Q1=6 and Q3=15, IQR=9. If min=2 and max=19, range=17. A sample of 40 scores has about 20 scores inside the box.
LESSON RECAP
A box plot shows minimum, Q1, median, Q3, maximum. The box contains the middle 50%; IQR=Q3−Q1; range=max−min. Read every length using the number-line units.
